extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, news organizations, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: A compact code of ethics for professional journalists describing principles and concrete practices for gathering, reporting, and presenting news responsibly. It covers truthfulness, minimizing harm, independence, and accountability with specific dos and don'ts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble — duty to public enlightenment
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Society of Professional Journalists believe that public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy. The duty of the journalist is to further those ends by seeking truth and providing a fair and comprehensive account of events and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes professional integrity, thoroughness, honesty and adoption of the code as principles and standards of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest, fair and courageous
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be honest, fair and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test accuracy of information; avoid error and distortion
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the accuracy of information from all sources and exercise care to avoid inadvertent error. Deliberate distortion is never permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all sourcing and fact-checking; intentional misrepresentation is expressly forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek response from subjects of allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek out subjects of news stories to give them the opportunity to respond to allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affords fairness and opportunity to comment prior to publication when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources whenever feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources whenever feasible. The public is entitled to as much information as possible on sources' reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about source identity and reliability supports public trust; anonymity only when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question motives before promising anonymity; keep promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Always question sources' motives before promising anonymity. Clarify conditions attached to any promise made in exchange for information. Keep promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires careful evaluation when granting anonymity and strict adherence to any agreed conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation in headlines and promotional material
rubrics_metrics.description: Make certain that headlines, news teases and promotional material, photos, video, audio, graphics, sound bites and quotations do not misrepresent. They should not oversimplify or highlight incidents out of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers all packaging and promotion of stories to prevent misleading the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not distort news photos or video; label montages
rubrics_metrics.description: Never distort the content of news photos or video. Image enhancement for technical clarity is always permissible. Label montages and photo illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits technical enhancement for clarity but requires labeling of altered or illustrative imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading re-enactments; label when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged news events. If re-enactment is necessary to tell a story, label it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If staging or re-enactment is used, clearly inform the audience to avoid deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undercover or surreptitious methods except when vital
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information except when traditional open methods will not yield information vital to the public. Use of such methods should be explained as part of the story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hidden newsgathering is a last resort and requires justification and transparency in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition; attribute others' work appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell diverse human stories boldly
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages coverage of underrepresented perspectives and challenging topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and avoid imposing cultural values
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine their own cultural values and avoid imposing those values on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-awareness about cultural bias is required to prevent imposition in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping by race, gender, age, religion, ethnicity, geography, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance or social status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit list of protected classes/qualities to avoid stereotyping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defend freedom of expression and include opposing or unpopular viewpoints where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Give voice to the voiceless; official and unofficial sources of information can be equally valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value both official and grassroots perspectives; aim for inclusive sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish advocacy from news; label analysis/commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between advocacy and news reporting. Analysis and commentary should be labeled and not misrepresent fact or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear labeling prevents conflation of opinion and factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising; shun hybrids
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid native advertising or sponsored content that masquerades as impartial news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure public business is open; seek access to records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open and that government records are open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists have a duty to pursue transparency and public records access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion for those harmed by coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected adversely by news coverage. Use special sensitivity when dealing with children and inexperienced sources or subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply heightened sensitivity for vulnerable populations and inexperienced interviewees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive around tragedy and grief
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive when seeking or using interviews or photographs of those affected by tragedy or grief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timing, method and necessity when approaching people in trauma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize reporting can cause harm; avoid arrogance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that gathering and reporting information may cause harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance public interest against potential harm; act with humility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect privacy of private people; intrude only for overriding public need
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than do public officials and others who seek power, influence or attention. Only an overriding public need can justify intrusion into anyone's privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher threshold for intruding into private individuals' lives; weigh public need carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show good taste; avoid pandering to lurid curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show good taste. Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalism that exploits subjects or audiences for shock value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious identifying juvenile suspects or sex-crime victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect identities when appropriate to prevent additional harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be judicious naming suspects before charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before the formal filing of charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider legal and ethical consequences of naming uncharged individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance fair-trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a criminal suspect's fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh reporting needs against potential prejudice to legal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain impartiality and prevent situations that could undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain free of compromising associations or activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain free of associations and activities that may compromise integrity or damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor outside affiliations and behavior that could impair journalistic objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse gifts, favors and compromising employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and shun secondary employment, political involvement, public office and service in community organizations if they compromise journalistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline benefits or roles that would create real or perceived obligations influencing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent with audiences about relationships or interests that could affect reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold the powerful accountable vigilantly
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively pursue oversight reporting on public officials and influential entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests and resist their pressure to influence news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve editorial independence from commercial pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of paid-for information; avoid bidding for news
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; avoid bidding for news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow monetary or transactional sourcing arrangements that bias reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and explain coverage; invite public dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and explain news coverage and invite dialogue with the public over journalistic conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage audiences, explain decisions and be open to discussion about journalistic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage public grievances against the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide channels for feedback and complaints to be heard and addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit mistakes and correct promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain credibility through timely and visible corrections and apologies when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical practices in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical practices of journalists and the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold the profession to its own standards by investigating misconduct within media organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by the same high standards applied to others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards to which they hold others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice the ethical conduct journalists demand of public figures and institutions.
